Subject: Control / Data Boundary Q&A + Egress Matrix (review requested)

Hi Daniel / Acme EdgeOps team —

Thanks again for the kickoff yesterday. Attaching a lightweight sketch of the control-plane / data-plane split we discussed and an initial egress port matrix for your infra team to validate. The two areas where we specifically need quick confirmation:

1) Can Acme allow egress from the inference nodes to the control-plane management IPs on TCP/443 and TCP/5222 (for our agent heartbeat)?
2) Will outbound traffic to telemetry.redwood.ai (443) be allowed for aggregated metrics and pull-based KV cache warm requests?

What I attached: control-data-boundary-sketch_v2.svg — shows the proposed NAT egress flow and NATlimiting tiering. egress-port-matrix.xlsx — proposed ports and CIDR destinations.

Please flag anything that won't work with your corporate egress policy or any local proxies we should be aware of. If helpful we can do a quick call tomorrow morning (30m) to walk the diagram.

Next steps after sign-off: ops will produce the runbook snippets (iptables rules, proxy config, and port tests) and we’ll schedule a smoke deploy into your staging VPC.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Product Solutions — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Control / Data Boundary Q&A + Egress Matrix (review requested)

Thanks Monica — quick read-through. A few comments inline: 

- Control-plane endpoints: prefer we pin the management endpoints to a small list of IPs / FQDNs and use mTLS in front of them. If Acme's network team requires, we can provide a short-lived cert rotation plan for the agent.
- Heartbeat port: 5222 is ok, but can we make heartbeats outbound-only from compute nodes (no inbound from internet)? That reduces their firewall scope.
- Telemetry: aggregated metrics to telemetry.redwood.ai are fine. If they route via a corporate proxy, we need the proxy host and a proxy-auth header sample so our collector can authenticate.

I updated the port matrix with a suggested conservative baseline (column "redwood-recommended"). See attached.

Irene
Sr. PM, Private Deploys
Redwood Inference

Adding a couple of infra-level notes from the ops side: 

- NAT behaviour: prefer source-NAT at edge to collapse ephemeral ports; we'll provide a test harness that hits our control-plane health-check endpoints so your team can confirm stateful NAT mappings remain sticky for 30s.
- Port tests: I'll attach a small bash snippet (tcping + curl) in the runbook. We'll need an outbound TLS-allowlist entry for the following hostnames: control1.redwood-internal.net, control2.redwood-internal.net, telemetry.redwood.ai, s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com (for optional snapshot upload).
- Egress throttling: If Acme enforces per-IP egress rate limits, we should plan for agent backoff and a fallback to local disk buffering for logs.

Monica / team — thanks for the clear doc and the suggested baseline. Acme agrees in principle with the split and the outbound-only requirement for agent heartbeats looks good to our security team. Two quick items before we sign off:

1) We route outbound through our corporate proxy (proxy.acme.local:3128) and use NTLM. Can you confirm the collector supports header-based proxy auth or if we need to terminate proxy at a local forwarder?
2) For the control-plane IPs, we cannot consume third-party FQDN allowlists; we require a CIDR block to be white-listed. Can you provide an expected /27 (or /26) range for the managed control-plane so our firewall team can create the rule?

If you can answer those two items we can finalize and schedule the staging deploy next week. Happy to do a 30m call Mon 9/14 at 09:00 PT if that helps.

Thanks —
Daniel Park
Head of Edge Infrastructure
Acme Robotics
